in_text_mentions: Intraoral examination revealed a bald tongue with a leukoplakic patch of size 3 × 4 cm. The depapillated regions were erythematous (Figure 2).

There was dryness of skin with reticular pigmentation on the sun exposed areas, especially the back and the neck, as well as the palms and soles since three years (Figure 2). She also had brittle and cracked nails which were painful and present for the same period (Figure 2). Occasionally, there was pus discharge from the nails which had been treated with antibiotics. There was associated sweating of palms and soles of feet. Patient had mild photophobia and epiphora. There was a significant alopecia of scalp over the past year.
